newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu condemns anti-Moslem posters in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu condemns anti-Moslem posters in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu called the Arab mayor of Hebron on Sunday to condemn the distribution there of posters depicting the Moslem Prophet Mohammad as a pig stomping on the Koran.
Hours after the phone call, Palestinians said Israeli troops entered a school in Hebron and scrawled anti-Arab slogans on blackboards. The army said it was checking the report.

A Jerusalem magistrate's court remanded for five days 25-year-old Jerusalem resident Tatyana Suskin suspected of pasting the posters on 20 storefronts near a Jewish settlement enclave in the West Bank, Israel's army radio said.

"I felt it necessary to call the mayor of Hebron to express not only my personal revulsion but the revulsion of the entire people of Israel," Netanyahu told Jewish leaders at a conference in Jerusalem.
"This runs counter to our outlook as Jews and our respect and appreciation for the Islamic religion and for its founder the Prophet Mohammad," he said.
Israeli President Ezer Weizman said the poster was an "idiotic, stupid" drawing.
Dozens of protesters took to the streets in Hebron on Saturday after Palestinian shopkeepers discovered the posters. Islam and Judaism view pigs as unclean and ban the eating of pork.

"It's connected with their views -- they don't want any Jews at all in Hebron or in this area whatsoever. It's unimportant how we will behave. They will demand more and more. I only say they are using their religion to force people to fight Jews," Suskin told the army radio.
Police said they arrested Suskin after she threw a rock through the windshield of an Arab's car in Hebron and found posters in her possession.

A Palestinian education official said teachers found the words "All Arabs are sons of whores, only border policemen are real men" written overnight on a blackboard in a school located near Jewish enclaves in the town.
"They also destroyed closets and shot at pictures of President Yasser Arafat," said Hebron eduction ministry director Mohammad Maswadeh.

Israel handed over most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule in January but kept troops in about 20 percent of the city to guard some 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city of 100,000 Palestinians.
The town has been the scene of clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops since Israel's groundbreaking in March on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem plunged peacemaking into crisis.
